queries: OpenAI "How people are using ChatGPT" study September 2025 practical guidance seeking information writing

sources_considered.why: Primary OpenAI/NBER study of what people use ChatGPT for and how use deepens over time. It is context only: it describes use but does not isolate media hype as a cause of growth, and it was published after the post.
Secondary coverage of the same OpenAI study; the primary source is preferred.

evidence_items.locator: section 'What they’re using it for', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: Three-quarters of conversations focus on practical guidance, seeking information, and writing—with writing being the most common work task, while coding and self-expression remain niche activities.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's own study describes what users do with ChatGPT. It shows task use and that OpenAI described uses after the post. It does not show whether media hype or usefulness drove growth, so it cannot settle the causal claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: And as people discover these and other benefits, usage deepens—with user cohorts increasing their activity over time through improved models and new use-case discovery.

evidence_items.explanation: This is OpenAI's own claim that use deepens among existing users. That cuts somewhat against a hype-only story, but it comes from the company, does not give cohort data here, and does not control for media exposure.

unresolved_gaps: No independent study was found that separates media attention from usefulness as drivers of ChatGPT's growth between Nov 2022 and May 2025.
OpenAI has not published cohort retention data that would show whether early, hype-era sign-ups stayed.
'Can't explain what it's for' has no measure, and OpenAI's main description of uses (Sept 2025) came after the post.
